title: Boss: the on-call shift
summary: Find runaway process trees, read the journal, and predict when cron fires next.

steps.title: Pager duty
steps.body: Three tickets are waiting. You'll need your cron matcher from the last lesson for the final one.

steps.title: Kill the whole tree
steps.prompt: A worker forks children that fork grandchildren. Killing only the parent leaves orphans. Write `List<int> Tree(List<(int Pid, int Ppid)> procs, int root)` returning `root` and **all** its descendants, in the order you'd want to SIGTERM them: **children before parents** (deepest first). Among siblings, lower PID first.
starter: List<int> Tree(List<(int Pid, int Ppid)> procs, int root)
solution: List<int> Tree(List<(int Pid, int Ppid)> procs, int root)
foreach (var child in procs.Where(p => p.Ppid == pid).Select(p => p.Pid).OrderBy(p => p))
hints: A post-order walk: visit all children, then add yourself.
Sort each node's children by PID before visiting them.

steps.title: Filter the journal
prompt: Write `List<string> JournalFilter(List<string> lines, string unit, string minPriority)`. Each line is `"<unit> <priority> <message>"`, e.g. `"orders-api err Unhandled exception"`. Return the **messages** for that unit whose priority is `minPriority` or **more severe**, like `journalctl -u unit -p minPriority`.
Severity order, most severe first: `emerg alert crit err warning notice info debug`.
starter: List<string> JournalFilter(List<string> lines, string unit, string minPriority)
solution: List<string> JournalFilter(List<string> lines, string unit, string minPriority)
hints: Put the levels in a list; a smaller index is more severe.
template: var dojoJ = new List<string> { "orders-api info Started", "orders-api err Unhandled exception", "nginx err upstream timed out", "orders-api crit Out of memory", "orders-api warning Slow query" };
Dojo.Eq("-p err", new List<string> { "Unhandled exception", "Out of memory" }, JournalFilter(dojoJ, "orders-api", "err"));
Dojo.Eq("-p warning", new List<string> { "Unhandled exception", "Out of memory", "Slow query" }, JournalFilter(dojoJ, "orders-api", "warning"));
Dojo.Eq("other unit", new List<string> { "upstream timed out" }, JournalFilter(dojoJ, "nginx", "debug"));

steps.title: When does the backup run next?
prompt: Someone asks "when will the backup run next?". Paste your `CronMatches` and write `DateTime NextRun(string expr, DateTime after)`: the first whole minute **strictly after** `after` that matches. Search at most one year ahead; you may assume a match exists.
Start from `after` with seconds dropped, plus one minute.
solution: return Field(f[0], t.Minute, 0) && Field(f[1], t.Hour, 0) && Field(f[2], t.Day, 1)
bool Field(string field, int value, int min)
if (slash >= 0) { range = part.Substring(0, slash); step = int.Parse(part.Substring(slash + 1)); }
else if (range.Contains('-')) { var b = range.Split('-'); lo = int.Parse(b[0]); hi = int.Parse(b[1]); }
else { lo = int.Parse(range); hi = slash >= 0 ? int.MaxValue : lo; }
if (value >= lo && value <= hi && (value - lo) % step == 0) return true;
var t = new DateTime(after.Year, after.Month, after.Day, after.Hour, after.Minute, 0).AddMinutes(1);
hints: Truncate seconds by building a new `DateTime` from its parts.
Step a minute at a time: at most ~525,000 checks, which is fast enough.
template: Dojo.Eq("daily 03:00", new DateTime(2031, 3, 11, 3, 0, 0), NextRun("0 3 * * *", new DateTime(2031, 3, 10, 3, 0, 0)));
Dojo.Eq("weekdays from Friday evening", new DateTime(2031, 3, 17, 9, 0, 0), NextRun("0 9 * * 1-5", new DateTime(2031, 3, 14, 18, 0, 0)));
Dojo.Eq("monthly", new DateTime(2031, 4, 1, 2, 30, 0), NextRun("30 2 1 * *", new DateTime(2031, 3, 1, 2, 30, 0)));
